atoms.text: This guide configures the replication role used by VaultSync to copy new objects from the bucket acme-prod-data to the bucket acme-dr-data, both in account 111122223333. The role is named vaultsync-replication-role, and its trust policy already lets the VaultSync service assume it. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to that role, and neither bucket policy is changed. In the role's policy, add a statement that allows s3:GetReplicationConfiguration and s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-prod-data. Add a second statement that allows s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication and s3:GetObjectVersionTagging on arn:aws:s3:::acme-prod-data/*. Add a third statement that allows s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::acme-dr-data/*. Save the policy and enable the replication rule with a 15-minute replication time target. Upload a test object to acme-prod-data and confirm that its replication status changes from PENDING to COMPLETED, then check that the replica in acme-dr-data has the same checksum as the source.

This guide configures the replication role used by VaultSync to copy new objects from the bucket acme-prod-data to the bucket acme-dr-data, both in account 111122223333. The role is named vaultsync-replication-role, and its trust policy already lets the VaultSync service assume it. Access is granted only by statements in the resource-based policies of the two buckets, and the role has no storage permissions in its own identity-based policy. In the bucket policy of acme-prod-data, add a statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/vaultsync-replication-role and that allows s3:GetReplicationConfiguration and s3:ListBucket on the bucket. Add a second statement with the same Principal that allows s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication and s3:GetObjectVersionTagging on arn:aws:s3:::acme-prod-data/*. In the bucket policy of acme-dr-data, add a statement with the same Principal that allows s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::acme-dr-data/*. Save both bucket policies and enable the replication rule with a 15-minute replication time target. Upload a test object to acme-prod-data and confirm that its replication status changes from PENDING to COMPLETED, then check that the replica in acme-dr-data has the same checksum as the source.

This guide lets the nightly database backup agent upload dump files to the bucket acme-db-backups. The agent runs on a backup host under the role dbbackup-agent-role in account 111122223333. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to that role, and the bucket policy of acme-db-backups stays unchanged. Add a statement to the role's policy that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-db-backups/db-dumps/*. Add a second statement that allows s3:AbortMultipartUpload and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on the same resource. Add a third statement that allows s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on arn:aws:s3:::acme-db-backups. Large dumps are split into 64 MiB parts, so incomplete uploads must be abortable by the same role. Run the agent manually once and verify that a file named with the current date appears under db-dumps/. Confirm that a write to any other prefix is denied.

This guide lets the nightly database backup agent upload dump files to the bucket acme-db-backups. The agent runs on a backup host under the role dbbackup-agent-role in account 111122223333. Access is granted only by statements in the bucket policy of acme-db-backups, and the role's identity-based policy contains no storage permissions. Add a statement to the bucket policy whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/dbbackup-agent-role and that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-db-backups/db-dumps/*. Add a second statement with the same Principal that allows s3:AbortMultipartUpload and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on the same resource. Add a third statement with the same Principal that allows s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on arn:aws:s3:::acme-db-backups. Large dumps are split into 64 MiB parts, so incomplete uploads must be abortable by the same role. Run the agent manually once and verify that a file named with the current date appears under db-dumps/. Confirm that a write to any other prefix is denied.

This guide gives the on-call engineer a read-only path to the bucket acme-archive-eu for quarterly restore drills. The engineer signs in as the IAM user dr-oncall-restore in account 111122223333. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to that user, and the bucket policy is not modified. Add a statement that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-archive-eu with a condition limiting s3:prefix to snapshots/. Add a second statement that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::acme-archive-eu/snapshots/*. Do not include any write or delete actions, because the drill only reads snapshot data. Sign in as the user and list the contents of snapshots/ to confirm the listing succeeds. Download one snapshot object and compare its checksum with the value recorded in the backup catalog. Confirm that an attempt to upload a file returns an access denied error.

Access is granted only by statements in the bucket policy of acme-archive-eu, and the user has no storage permissions in an identity-based policy. Add a statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/dr-oncall-restore and that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-archive-eu with a condition limiting s3:prefix to snapshots/. Add a second statement with the same Principal that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::acme-archive-eu/snapshots/*. Do not include any write or delete actions, because the drill only reads snapshot data. Sign in as the user and list the contents of snapshots/ to confirm the listing succeeds. Download one snapshot object and compare its checksum with the value recorded in the backup catalog. Confirm that an attempt to upload a file returns an access denied error.

This guide sets up the verification job that checks backup integrity in the bucket acme-backup-vault. The job runs as the role backup-verifier-role in account 111122223333. It reads backup objects under snapshots/ and writes its result files under verification-reports/. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is left as it is. Add a statement that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-backup-vault and s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-backup-vault/snapshots/*. Add a second statement that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-backup-vault/verification-reports/*. Schedule the job to run daily after the replication window closes. After the first run, open the newest report in verification-reports/ and confirm it lists each snapshot with a matching checksum. Confirm that the role cannot overwrite or delete objects under snapshots/.

This guide sets up the verification job that checks backup integrity in the bucket acme-backup-vault. The job runs as the role backup-verifier-role in account 111122223333. It reads backup objects under snapshots/ and writes its result files under verification-reports/. Access is granted only by statements in the bucket policy of acme-backup-vault, and the role has no storage permissions in its identity-based policy. Add a statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/backup-verifier-role and that allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket and s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-backup-vault/snapshots/*. Add a second statement with the same Principal that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-backup-vault/verification-reports/*. Schedule the job to run daily after the replication window closes. After the first run, open the newest report in verification-reports/ and confirm it lists each snapshot with a matching checksum. Confirm that the role cannot overwrite or delete objects under snapshots/.

This guide authorizes the retention cleanup task that removes expired backup versions from the bucket acme-backup-vault. The task runs as the role backup-retention-role in account 111122223333 and has versioning enabled on the bucket. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is not changed. Add a statement that allows s3:ListBucketVersions on arn:aws:s3:::acme-backup-vault with a condition limiting s3:prefix to backups/. Add a second statement that allows s3:DeleteObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::acme-backup-vault/backups/*. Do not grant s3:DeleteObject without a version ID, so the task cannot create delete markers over current backups. Configure the task to delete only noncurrent versions older than 35 days. Run it in dry-run mode first and review the list of versions it would remove. Then run it for real and confirm that the current version of each backup object is still present.

This guide connects an on-premises backup appliance to the bucket acme-offsite-copies for offsite copies of file server backups. The appliance authenticates with the access key of the IAM user appliance-backup-writer in account 111122223333. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to that user, and the bucket policy is not modified. Add a statement that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-offsite-copies/appliance01/*. Add a second statement that allows s3:AbortMultipartUpload and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on the same resource, together with s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on arn:aws:s3:::acme-offsite-copies. Do not allow s3:GetObject, because the appliance only writes and never reads back. Enter the access key in the appliance console and set the target bucket and the appliance01/ prefix. Start a test job that copies a 1 GiB file and check that the object appears with the expected size. Rotate the access key every 90 days.

The appliance authenticates with the access key of the IAM user appliance-backup-writer in account 111122223333. Access is granted only by statements in the bucket policy of acme-offsite-copies, and the user has no storage permissions in an identity-based policy. Add a statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/appliance-backup-writer and that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-offsite-copies/appliance01/*. Add a second statement with the same Principal that allows s3:AbortMultipartUpload and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on the same resource, together with s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket. Do not allow s3:GetObject, because the appliance only writes and never reads back. Enter the access key in the appliance console and set the target bucket and the appliance01/ prefix. Start a test job that copies a 1 GiB file and check that the object appears with the expected size. Rotate the access key every 90 days.

This guide prepares the failover promotion role that reads replicated data in the recovery region during a disaster recovery event. The role, named dr-failover-role in account 111122223333, reads from the replica bucket acme-dr-data and copies objects into the staging bucket acme-restore-staging. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to the role, and neither bucket policy is changed. Add a statement that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-dr-data. Add a second statement that allows s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersion and s3:GetObjectTagging on arn:aws:s3:::acme-dr-data/*. Add a third statement that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-restore-staging/*. The role must not be able to modify objects in acme-dr-data, so the replicas remain unchanged. Run the failover runbook in the test environment and confirm that the staged objects match the replicas by checksum. Record the elapsed copy time in the runbook.

This guide prepares the failover promotion role that reads replicated data in the recovery region during a disaster recovery event. The role, named dr-failover-role in account 111122223333, reads from the replica bucket acme-dr-data and copies objects into the staging bucket acme-restore-staging. Access is granted only by statements in the bucket policies of the two buckets, and the role has no storage permissions in its identity-based policy. In the bucket policy of acme-dr-data, add a statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/dr-failover-role and that allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket. Add a second statement with the same Principal that allows s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersion and s3:GetObjectTagging on arn:aws:s3:::acme-dr-data/*. In the bucket policy of acme-restore-staging, add a statement with the same Principal that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-restore-staging/*. The role must not be able to modify objects in acme-dr-data, so the replicas remain unchanged. Run the failover runbook in the test environment and confirm that the staged objects match the replicas by checksum. Record the elapsed copy time in the runbook.

This guide restricts a tenant-specific backup agent to its own prefix in the shared bucket acme-tenant-backups. The agent runs as the role tenant042-backup-role in account 111122223333 and must write only under tenants/tenant-042/. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the shared bucket policy is not changed. Add a statement that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-tenant-backups/tenants/tenant-042/*. Add a condition to this statement requiring s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption to equal AES256, so that unencrypted uploads are rejected. Add a second statement that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-tenant-backups with a condition limiting s3:prefix to tenants/tenant-042/. Configure the agent to send the server-side encryption header with every request. Upload a test archive with the header and confirm that it succeeds. Upload one without the header and confirm that it is denied.

Add a statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/tenant042-backup-role and that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-tenant-backups/tenants/tenant-042/*. Add a condition to this statement requiring s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption to equal AES256, so that unencrypted uploads are rejected. Add a second statement with the same Principal that allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a condition limiting s3:prefix to tenants/tenant-042/. Configure the agent to send the server-side encryption header with every request. Upload a test archive with the header and confirm that it succeeds. Upload one without the header and confirm that it is denied.
